newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end stronger, lifted by New York.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end stronger, lifted by New York.

text.p: Toronto stocks ended Thursday on a firmer note, aided by strength on Wall Street and declining interest rate hike fears.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index added 28.47 points to reach 6276.65. Trading was active at 94.9 million shares worth C$1.5 billion.
New York rose 47.39 points to close at 7333.55.

Toronto's influential banking sector rose more than one percent after North American investors decided that the chance of a U.S. interest rate hike still remained low, said Dunnery Best, Midland Walwyn's director of private client investing.
U.S. April consumer prices rose 0.1 percent as expected, but the core rate rose 0.3 percent against forecasts of a 0.2 percent increase.

Best also credited Canada's strong fundamentals, underlined in comments made by Bank of Canada Governor Gord Thiessen on Thursday. Thiessen said the solid outlook for profits was reflected in Toronto's climbing stock prices and he forecast a stronger Canadian dollar.
Eleven of Toronto's 14 sub-indexes rose, including banks, real estate, golds and oils. The three declining groups were conglomerates, transportation and media.
Advancing issues outweighed decliners 546 to 427 and 305 were flat.

* Shares in Gandalf Technologies Inc tumbled 34 percent or 0.83 to 1.61 on 1.7 million shares. Late on Wednesday, the networking firm reported that it was seeking additional financing after its major bank forgave a loan default but lowered Gandalf's credit facility.
Losses in the past two days wiped out the 150 percent gains Gandalf shares made on Tuesday.
